chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid said, on the authority of some of our scholars, that Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) passed by a grave from the graves of his Household, so he placed his hand on it, and then said:

O my God! Your Omnipotence is apparent, but Your Essence/Shape is not apparent, so they were ignorant of You and tried to measure You. And any measurement of You is other than what is in You. And I am free from those who sought You through comparison (anthropomorphism). Nothing is similar to You, O my God. And they will not comprehend You. And the apparent blessings upon them from You are their proof for You, if they knew You. And in Your creation, O my God, there is sufficiency that they should grasp You. But they equated You with Your creation, from which they did not know You. And they took some of Your signs as a lord, and for that reason they described You. You are exalted, O my Lord, from what the anthropomorphists described You with.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological perspective on divine attributes and anthropomorphism according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This supplication by Imam al-Rida (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih) by distinguishing between God's manifest power (qudrah) and His unseen essence (dhat), critiquing anthropomorphists who limit the Divine through human categories. It emphasizes that while creation serves as a pointer to God, finite minds often mistake the signs for the Signifier, leading to misdescription. This text is pivotal in understanding the theological nuance between knowing God through His attributes versus knowing His essence, a key theme in Shia kalam.
